cards.explanation: The word is conceited. Paul, the apostle who wrote this letter to the believers in Rome, says he tells them this mystery “…so that you will not be conceited…”. Earlier he had already told the Gentiles not to boast over the branches (Romans 11:18). I think this mystery is a good cure for a swelled head, friends.

What has come to Israel in part is a hardening. Paul says, “A hardening in part has come to Israel…” Notice the words in part, friends. It's not the whole story, and Paul says it lasts only until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.

The answer is False. The hardening will not last forever. Paul says it has come in part, “…until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.” That's a time limit, not a forever. Then in the next verse he goes straight to all Israel being saved.

The big statement is that all Israel will be saved. Paul says, “And so all Israel will be saved…” It fits what he asked earlier, when he said God has not rejected His people (Romans 11:1). I think that's good news worth reading twice, friends.

The answer is True. The Scripture goes on, “And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.” Notice the when, friends. The covenant is tied to God taking their sins away. That line runs right on from the Deliverer coming from Zion (Romans 11:26).

The answer is the patriarchs. Paul says that regarding election, they are loved on account of the patriarchs. He has just said that regarding the gospel they are enemies on the Gentiles' account. So he's showing two sides, and this is the loved side.

The answer is False. God does not take back His gifts and His call. Paul says, “For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.” Irrevocable is a big word that means they can't be called back. I once got a refund on a bag of chocolate chips, friends, but God's gifts don't work like that.

The word is disobedience. Paul says, “Just as you who formerly disobeyed God have now received mercy through their disobedience…” So the Gentiles in Rome received mercy through Israel's disobedience. It's a surprising turn, friends, and Paul just says it plainly.

The answer is the mercy shown to the Gentiles. Paul says they too have now disobeyed, “…in order that they too may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to you.” It goes both ways, friends. Mercy came to the Gentiles through Israel's disobedience (Romans 11:30), and now Israel may receive mercy through the mercy shown to the Gentiles.

The answer is True. Paul says, “For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.” Notice that it says everyone twice, friends. This is his summary after explaining how Gentiles and Israel both come to mercy.

The answer is False. No amount of study traces out all of God's ways. Paul says, “How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!” Those two words, unsearchable and untraceable, say it clearly. I've read a lot of recipes, friends, but even I can't trace out the ways of God.

The answer Paul expects is no one. He asks, “Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?” The questions are meant to be answered with no one, friends. He is quoting the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 40:13).

The answer is False. Paul's point is that God owes no one. He asks, “Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?” (Romans 11:35). It expects the answer no one, so there's no one God owes. Paul follows it with, “For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things.”
The answer is God. Paul says, “To Him be the glory forever! Amen.” He has just said that from Him and through Him and to Him are all things, friends. So the glory goes to God.
